citation: Ibero-Baraibar I, Suárez M, Arola-Arnal A, Zulet MA, Martínez JA. Cocoa extract intake for 4 weeks reduces postprandial systolic blood pressure response of obese subjects, even after following an energy-restricted diet. Food Nutr Res. 2016;60:30449.
protocol: Ready-to-eat test meal (courgette cream 300 g and chocolate custard 150 g; 365 kcal: 34.2 g carbohydrate, 20.9 g lipids, 8.9 g protein) with 1.4 g cocoa extract or without (control meal), on day 1 and day 28 of a 4-week diet; BP at 0, 60, 120 and 180 min; glucose and insulin as AUC.
population: Substudy of 24 volunteers, 12 control (6 M, 6 F) and 12 cocoa (5 M, 7 F) at allocation; 11 cocoa analysed in tables; age 58.2 +/- 5.2 y; BMI 30.2 (SD 2.2) control, 31.4 (SD 2.6) cocoa; overweight or obese (inclusion BMI 27.0-35.5, age 50-80), no disease stated.
note: Obese, not diseased, so kept as mixed. The control arm (same meal, no cocoa) is the usable comparator. Values are unadjusted mean (SD) AUCs, not timepoint means; insulin AUC is non-normal per the footnote, so SD is a poor spread, and no medians are printed. Cocoa arm n=11 in tables though 12 allocated.
